headline: Bitcoin holds near $81,800 as Nasdaq futures slide and Brent tops $112
summary: Wall Street closed higher Wednesday (Nasdaq +1.05%, S&P 500 +0.58%, TSX +0.60%), but Thursday looks weak: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.7–1.9% and S&P 500 futures about 1.1% before the open, with IBM off about 6%, Tesla about 5% and Lam Research about 8% after earnings that revived doubts about AI spending. Bitcoin is near $81,800, down about 2% in a day after a round trip to nearly $85,000, while altcoins fare worse and bitcoin's share of the crypto market sits near 59–60%, its highest since May. U.S. crude is near $99.50 and Brent above $112 on fresh Middle East supply fears, keeping inflation worries alive ahead of next week's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions; weekly U.S. jobless claims are due at 8:30 a.m. ET.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Fear & Greed still reads 68 (Greed), but bitcoin is down about 2% and ether about 2.6% on the day, total crypto value is down about 4.4% to $2.76 trillion, and only a few coins such as Monero and Lighter are rising.

stocks.label: Risk-off
stocks.why: Wednesday's close was strong, but S&P 500 futures were down about 1.1% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 1.7–1.9% early Thursday after a roughly 3% slide in Asia, with the VIX fear gauge up about 9% to 18.2 and oil climbing.

drivers.title: AI-spending jitters after Big Tech earnings
drivers.detail: Before the open, Tesla was down about 5%, IBM about 6% (its CEO said corporate clients are questioning AI returns), Intel about 5% and Lam Research about 9%, with AMD, Broadcom, Micron and other chipmakers off 3–5% and Meta about 2% lower, as Tesla's capex cut and Meta's spending plans revived doubts about the payoff from AI. The worry spread across Asia and Europe: Korea's Kospi fell 3.5%, Japan's Nikkei about 2.7%, Hong Kong more than 2%, China's CSI 300 entered a bear market, and the Stoxx 600 slipped about 0.9%.

drivers.title: Stablecoin rules finalized
drivers.detail: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a top U.S. bank regulator, finalized reserve, redemption and risk rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027. Circle rose about 6%, Coinbase about 4–5% and Strategy about 8%, though whether exchanges can keep paying stablecoin 'rewards' is still unsettled.

drivers.title: High yields and a Fed on hold
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield has eased to about 5.08% from 5.15% at Wednesday's close as nervous investors buy bonds, but it is still near its highest levels in years after September CPI ran hot at 3.7%. CME FedWatch puts the odds of a hold at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28 at about 87%, though traders still see a real chance of a hike later this year.

drivers.title: Oil climbs on Saudi attacks
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 2.4% to roughly $99.50 a barrel and Brent is around $112, its highest since May, after Iran-aligned Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and the Shaybah oil field; the U.S. also told staff to leave its Riyadh embassy, and reports say the U.S. and Israel may resume strikes on Iran after the midterms. Higher oil feeds inflation fears, while gold is down about 1.4% to near $4,090.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, bonds, crypto

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETF buying is back, but modest
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $1.08 billion over their latest three days, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. CoinDesk notes past strong rallies came with steadier daily buying of about $200–$300 million, so the flows help but are not yet at rally pace.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada expected to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased. Economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28, which supported bank stocks today.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 2.0% in 24h, up 0.9% this week, to about $81,803 (down 5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday as tech stocks rallied, then fell as much as 2.9% to about $81,600, its biggest drop in two weeks, as Tesla's and Meta's results revived doubts about AI spending and Nasdaq futures slid. The round trip caused about $431 million of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically), split fairly evenly between bullish and bearish bets, and open interest fell, meaning traders were closing positions rather than adding new ones. Spot bitcoin ETFs still took in more than $1 billion over the first three days of the week. Separately, Chinese prosecutors are seeking to confiscate more than 61,800 BTC tied to a fraud case; the coins are held in Britain and tied up in court, so no sale is imminent.
crypto.meaning: The quick give-back shows buyers aren't yet strong enough to push it out of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying of about $1.08 billion over three days helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $70,000.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A weak U.S. open for tech, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher yields and oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: How tech stocks trade at Thursday's open, the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, daily ETF flows, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 2.6% in 24h, up 1.4% this week, to about $2,403 (down 13% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back overnight and dipped just under $2,400, and it keeps trailing as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network, though the average staking yield slipped to 2.63%.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Continued outflows or a broad risk-off turn could keep it below $2,400 and send it toward the $2,300 area; it slipped just under that level this morning.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, and the ETH/BTC ratio.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: Up 5.8% in 24h, up 17.5% this week, to about $639.13 (up 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, is the only large coin posting a big gain today, trading near $640. There is no project-specific news behind it: the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance. The run started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading volume has outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, a sign that leveraged bets are doing much of the lifting. Futures funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) are running near 70% a year, far above other coins, per CoinDesk, which shows how crowded the bullish side is.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds $600, futures open interest and funding rates, spot volume versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 1.9% in 24h, up 14.9% this week, to about $1,261 (down 17% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders are positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) rose about 19–24%, and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Bitwise's Zcash ETF saw small inflows Tuesday after outflows the day before. Today, open interest is falling faster than the price (about 7% vs. 2%), a sign some of those leveraged traders are taking profits.
crypto.meaning: Much of this rally is driven by leverage, and data show sellers stayed active during the rise, so swings both ways can be sharp. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour.

outlook.bullCase: Clearing resistance near $1,375 could bring the September high around $1,700 into view as the upgrade nears.
outlook.bearCase: Leveraged longs getting flushed could pull it back to the $1,190–$1,230 support area, and losing $1,180 would erase the breakout.
outlook.watch: $1,375 resistance, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Up 8.7% in 24h, up 25.5% this week, to about $3.71 (down 23% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The token of the Lighter derivatives exchange jumped after reports from its Oct. 21 investor call that it plans to apply for a U.S. licence in November and is weighing access through Robinhood's U.S. platform; neither has been confirmed. Renewed attention on its existing Robinhood Wallet partnership and a Delphi Digital research report added interest.
crypto.meaning: The move rests on unconfirmed plans. Only 25% of the 1 billion tokens are circulating, so future supply is a long-term overhang, and the token is still about half its all-time high.

outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.
outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or profit-taking after a 20% day, could send it back toward $3.20, the bottom of today's range.
outlook.watch: Official statements from Lighter, trading volume versus Hyperliquid, and token unlock schedules.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Down 4.1% in 24h, up 8.9% this week, to about $5.01 (up 10% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. It led the CoinDesk 100 on Wednesday without a single fresh headline, and is giving some of that back today with the wider market.
crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If momentum fades or the proposal stalls, a pullback toward roughly $4.50–$5.00 would be typical after a run this size.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether $5 holds.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Down 4.2% in 24h, up 7.4% this week, to about $0.200 (down 5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: ENA led large-cap gainers on Wednesday, then became one of the biggest losers today as DeFi tokens led crypto lower, with CoinDesk's DeFi index down about 6% and ENA about 25% below its late-September peak. The earlier rally looked driven by momentum, with the hourly RSI (a gauge of how overstretched a move is) hitting about 73, an overbought reading. A longer-term support is that the last tranche of early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, ending Ethena's monthly investor unlocks.
crypto.meaning: With the investor unlock overhang gone, ENA's supply picture is cleaner, but USDe, the synthetic dollar that drives Ethena's revenue, is far below its 2025 peak. A one-day pop on no clear news can unwind just as fast.

outlook.bullCase: A sustained move above about $0.2165, with USDe supply growing again, could carry ENA toward the mid-$0.20s.
outlook.bearCase: If the overbought bounce fades, a drop under about $0.195 (its 50-day average) would erase this week's gains.
outlook.watch: USDe supply, the $0.195–$0.2165 range, and broader altcoin risk appetite.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Down 2.2% in 24h, up 1.4% this week, to about $1.33 (down 13% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP is drifting lower with the rest of the market after a brief bounce on Wednesday. On the network side, a planned XRP Ledger bug fix was pushed back to November after support from validators (the computers that approve changes) briefly dipped, per a CoinDesk headline. Ripple's push to offer round-the-clock stock trading on crypto rails remains in the news, but no single catalyst explains today's move.
crypto.meaning: XRP tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions, so it mostly reflects overall risk appetite. The 30-day trend is still down about 14%, and the delayed ledger fix is a minor technical setback rather than a security event.

outlook.bullCase: A broader crypto rally led by bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 could lift XRP back toward the $1.45–$1.50 area.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin breaks below $80,000, XRP would likely lose the $1.30 area and could test about $1.20.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, the rescheduled XRP Ledger fix in November, and U.S. digital-asset rules.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 2.4% in 24h, up 2.1% this week, to about $104.38 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved roughly in line with the market rather than rallying on the news, slipping about 3% at one point overnight.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin break below $80,000, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000–$85,000 range, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed up 0.5% at $697.52; an after-hours jump of as much as 6% on earnings has turned into a loss of about 2% before Thursday's open
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating the roughly $63.3 billion expected, and earnings were $7.40 a share excluding a $9.9 billion legal charge ($3.83 including it). Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $73–$76 billion has a midpoint above consensus, and Meta narrowed 2026 capital spending to $135–$145 billion (raising the low end) while giving no 2027 number yet beyond saying AI investment stays heavy. It also plans to hand out one new non-voting Class C share for every existing share in January 2027, which works like a 2-for-1 split.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: If buyers return to the strong ad growth and analysts lift targets, it could recover toward the $740–$780 range it held earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended 2027 spending, the tech sell-off, or more legal costs could send it toward $670–$680.
outlook.watch: Thursday's trading, analyst target changes, and 2027 spending commentary.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed up 3.4% at $386.47; down about 5% before Thursday's open (near $367) after earnings
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares first rose about 2%, then turned lower during the call as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which is what the pre-market selling suggests.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the pre-market drop holds and analysts trim targets, it could slide toward $355.
outlook.watch: Thursday's open, analyst target changes, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: Lam Research

stocks.why: The chip-equipment maker reported revenue of $8.22 billion, up 54% from a year ago, and adjusted earnings of $2.20 a share, both ahead of forecasts. outlook.bearCase: If the after-hours loss holds and other chip-equipment makers guide cautiously, the selling could spread to the wider chip sector.
outlook.watch: Thursday's open, peers' results (KLA, Applied Materials), and Big Tech capital spending plans.

stocks.name: Strategy

stocks.meaning: MSTR is effectively a leveraged bet on bitcoin, so it amplifies both gains and losses. Its moves today say more about bitcoin than about the company.

outlook.bullCase: Bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 and moving toward $87,500 could lift MSTR toward the $165 area.
outlook.bearCase: A bitcoin break below $82,400 would likely send MSTR back under $140; with bitcoin back near $82,800, an early pullback Thursday is possible.

stocks.move: Flat at C$76.20, near its 52-week high of C$77.49 on Wednesday
stocks.why: Canada's largest oil producer closed flat Wednesday near record levels. Oil has kept climbing overnight, with U.S. crude near $100 and Brent above $112, its highest since May, after more Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, which could lift energy stocks when Toronto opens.
stocks.meaning: CNQ's fortunes track oil prices closely. Note: the U.S. oil price on our dashboard looks down about 4% today, but that mainly reflects the switch to the December contract, not a real drop.

outlook.bullCase: Continued Middle East tension keeping Brent above $105 could push CNQ to new highs above C$77.50.
outlook.bearCase: A credible Iran deal that sends oil sharply lower would hit CNQ, possibly back toward C$70–C$72.
outlook.watch: Iran–U.S. talks, Brent crude, and weekly U.S. oil inventories.

newCoins.name: Pearl
newCoins.what: A Bitcoin-style blockchain launched in April 2026 whose mining is meant to do AI-style math (matrix multiplication) instead of pure puzzle-solving.
newCoins.why: It is trending and in the top 100 at about $2.25: down about 2% today but up about 34% this week and 130% over 30 days, riding the 'useful AI mining' story.
newCoins.redFlags: A researcher found the main mining software contained no actual AI code, and a co-founder admitted miners can 'spam mine'. Supply grows by about 1 million tokens a day, roughly doubling over the next year. It trades on very few exchanges with thin liquidity.

newCoins.name: Midnight
newCoins.what: A privacy-focused blockchain linked to Cardano; its v8 upgrade lets developers build private smart contracts and tokens.
newCoins.why: NIGHT has rebounded on the upgrade, up about 66% over 30 days to roughly $0.040 and in the top 100, though it is down about 6% this week.
newCoins.redFlags: About 515 million NIGHT were stolen in a July bridge hack. Airdrop ('Glacier Drop') claims keep unlocking until early December, which could add selling pressure, and about 7 billion of 24 billion tokens are not yet circulating.

newCoins.name: Axis Robotics
newCoins.what: A 'physical AI' data project that sold tokens to the public in late September at $0.10 each on the Base network.
newCoins.why: It is trending on CoinGecko at about $0.28, well above its sale price, with a market value near $47 million.
newCoins.redFlags: Very new with little track record. 75% of sale tokens unlock after a six-month cliff, which could add selling pressure later. Official launch and listing details have been unclear, so double-check contract addresses before using any wallet.

newCoins.name: Doodles
newCoins.what: The Solana token of the Doodles NFT (digital collectible) brand.
newCoins.why: It was among the day's top gainers on several trackers earlier, more than doubling in 24 hours, with no clear project-specific reason reported.
newCoins.redFlags: A tiny market value (tens of millions of dollars) means small trades move the price a lot. No specific catalyst was reported, and spikes like this often reverse within days.
